adjudication_rationale: Proposes dynamic lane assignment, gridlock metering and diversion, and argues their effects from theory and earlier observations. No strategy is evaluated and no AV/CAV control is involved.
MPC merging is shown for isolated three-vehicle manoeuvres with no uncontrolled comparator and no delay, throughput or congestion metric. This supports a control principle, not a congestion outcome.
The controller is infrastructure variable speed limits with no AV/CAV actuation or share, so it supports the inflow-regulation principle rather than an AV/CAV claim.
Q-learning variable speed limits at a merge bottleneck are infrastructure control with no AV/CAV actuation or share.
Collision-free coordinated merging of a few CAVs in five short runs, with no baseline and no traffic-flow metric; it shows trajectory feasibility only.
Both coders coded [M] (second author [M][F]). The paper derives the CACC string-stability region under communication delay and reports no congestion outcome.
Derives analytical string-stability and capacity conditions for mixed CACC-ACC-human flow. No breakdown, queue or wave is simulated or measured.
Estimates lane capacity under ACC/CACC penetration; no bottleneck, breakdown, queue or wave is simulated. Capacity enters as a mechanism input, not a congestion outcome.

Simulates a single-lane highway with an on-ramp and reports breakdown flow and maximum throughput rising with CV/AV penetration, alongside analytical string stability. This directly evaluates an AV/CAV congestion claim, as do Shang and Stern (2021) and van Arem et al. (2006), which both coders kept as [D]. The audit reassessment to [M] is reversed.
Reports only RL reward, comfort and illustrative lane-change snapshots, with no speed, delay, throughput or congestion metric and no non-RL baseline. Reward gains are not a traffic outcome.
Q-learning mainline speed limits reduce off-ramp queue overflow, but the control is infrastructure speed limits simulated without a CAV share. It supports spillback control, not an AV/CAV claim.
